title: Availability degradation crediting and automatic route reshuffle policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently lack a unified decision policy that (1) credits tenants for short, tolerated degradations without burning their primary error budget, (2) automatically reshuffles request routing during region or variant strain, and (3) exposes predictable hysteresis for circuit breakers so downstream consumers avoid oscillation. This ticket defines the policy, acceptance criteria, and an implementation sketch for per-endpoint availability degradation credits and the automatic route reshuffle controller.

Goals: 1) Define a degradation-credit unit (DCU) that maps brief availability dips to refundable credits instead of immediate error-budget burn, with clear redemption semantics. 2) Specify token-length-normalized latency and quality SLIs so reshuffle decisions prioritize routes by true user impact. 3) Define circuit-breaker thresholds with warm/cool windows and additive backoff to prevent thrashing during regional recoveries. 4) Produce a rollout plan and observability requirements (dashboards, alerts, test harness).

Key definitions: - Degradation Credit Unit (DCU): one DCU = 1s of median route latency over baseline weighted by request importance. DCUs can be auto-refunded if degraded window < 30s and root cause is transient. - Token-normalized Latency SLI: p95 latency per 1k tokens to normalize conversational and long-context routes. - Quality Delta SLI: a promptset-linked metric (e.g., hallucination rate or BLEU-like score) with a 14-day rolling baseline used to detect regression-driven degradations.

High-level policy rules: 1) If a route exceeds its latency or quality SLI for > 10s but < 30s, convert the incident into DCUs rather than immediate error-budget charge. DCUs are stored on the endpoint ledger and automatically applied to the next maintenance or billing reconciliation. 2) If the same route exceeds SLI for > 30s, begin progressive load shedding and mark as error-budget burn after an initial DCU deduction equal to the observed degradation. 3) Automatic route reshuffle: when a regional capacity signal crosses a threshold (capacity-utilization > 85% for 20s or instance error rate > 3% for 15s), the reshuffle controller evaluates candidate fallback variants by composite score (latency per token, quality delta, tenant priority) and shifts a configurable % of traffic in 5s windows with a 60s cooldown. 4) Circuit breakers expose three states: Closed, Open, and Backoff. Backoff is additive and grows with number of consecutive failures; a successful cool-window resets backoff to base.

Trade-offs considered: - DCU model increases complexity in billing reconciliation but prevents unnecessary long-term customer impact from transient spikes. - Token-normalized SLIs increase computational cost in telemetry but improve fairness across routes. - Shorter cooldowns reduce user-visible latency improvements but risk oscillation; hence the chosen 60s rounded cooldown with conservative initial shifts.

Implementation sketch: Phase 1 (policy + telemetry): finalize DCU math, extend tracing to attach token counts, implement Quality Delta pipelines for linked promptsets, and add dashboard panels. Phase 2 (controller + sim): build reshape controller as independent service with canary traffic switcher and simulated failure harness; add circuit breaker state machine to runtime agents. Phase 3 (rollout): gated rollout by percentage and tenant priority, monitor burn rates and regression alerts, and enable DCU reconciliation in billing batch.

Acceptance criteria: - A formal DCU spec document published in Confluence with reconciliation examples. - Token-normalized p95 telemetry emitted for all routes and visible in Console panels. - Reshuffle controller prototype can re-route 20% of traffic with no more than 1% increase in error-rate on fallback routes during synthetic degradation tests. - Circuit-breaker hysteresis prevents oscillation in synthetic failure + recovery scenarios for at least 5 consecutive test runs.

Dependencies: this work depends on the telemetry-enrichment (ENG-65412) and the billing-ledger API (ENG-70123).

risks: DCU refund edge cases may cause billing disputes; reshuffle may expose fallback variants to unexpected traffic patterns causing quality regressions; token-counting overhead could increase ingestion costs.
